issuer: Driver and Vehicle Licensing, Isle of Man Government (Driver and Vehicle Test Centre, Tromode)
note: The Isle of Man Government's pages, read 2026-10-30 and again 2026-11-03. Driving licences, age related licence applications: a motor car (with a goods vehicle up to 3050 kg unladen) from age 16. The full licence follows the test with no minimum time on the provisional licence stated; for its first 12 months it is a restricted full licence (R plates, 50 mph; New drivers, regulation 9 of the Driving Licences and Test Regulations 2007), so 16 is held as the full licence's age. Until 2026-11-03 this was a reading held back as the blocker papers.licence.blocked.IM, the table giving the age for a licence for the class, not for the full licence by name; that day the Department of Infrastructure's commissioned report (TRL, PPR952, 2020) was read: it counts young drivers 'aged 16-24 years old' holding 'a full car licence', calls 16 the island's licensing age, and treats a minimum learner period only as a proposal, which settled the reading. Costs as at 1 May 2023: a full licence for someone aged under 66 costs £45 and is valid 10 years (shorter and cheaper from 66, £14 for three years from 72), held; the first provisional licence (£14) isn't. The Regulations themselves (legislation.gov.im) still answered 'Request Rejected' (a web application firewall) on 2026-11-03 and weren't read. No identity card is held; the exchange lists weren't read.
